canonical.title: MUI vs shadcn/ui vs Mantine vs Base UI: the 2026 maturity and governance baseline

parent.title: Which React UI component kit should itenium-ui adopt in 2026?

siblings.title: Styling engine and Tailwind 4 interop: which React component kit survives the cascade
siblings.summary: Tailwind 4 puts every utility inside a cascade layer, so any kit that ships unlayered CSS silently outranks it — which reframes the MUI/shadcn/Mantine/Base UI choice as a question about where each kit's styles land in the layer stack, and surfaces a bigger Nx @source tax underneath all four.

siblings.title: Admin-console component coverage: what MUI, shadcn/ui, Mantine and Base UI actually ship in 2026
siblings.summary: Only Mantine covers a CRUD admin console in-box with a single gap (the data grid); MUI's coverage is real but the grid features you actually need are paywalled; shadcn now defaults to Base UI, making them one choice, not two.

siblings.title: A11y & primitive foundations: what MUI, shadcn/ui, Mantine and Base UI actually inherit in 2026
siblings.summary: shadcn-vs-Base-UI is a false dichotomy: since July 2026 shadcn/ui ships Base UI as its default primitive layer, so the real choice is which primitive foundation you inherit — and none of the four kits publishes a VPAT.

siblings.title: Theming, tokens and brand reach: MUI vs shadcn/ui vs Mantine vs Base UI in 2026
siblings.summary: On a Tailwind-4 monorepo the token substrate decides the kit: shadcn/ui and Base UI put brand tokens directly in @theme, while MUI and Mantine keep a JS theme object as the source of truth and only emit CSS variables downstream.

siblings.title: Nx 21 build ergonomics: which UI kit survives a shared itenium-ui library
siblings.summary: shadcn/ui's copy-in model does work in a shared Nx library, but only if you own the plumbing: a components.json in the lib, a private registry for updates, and Tailwind 4 @source globs across the boundary.

sources.title: mui/material-ui — GitHub
sources.claim: Material UI repo health as of 14 Jul 2026: 98,582 stars, MIT, 1,387 open issues, 113 opened / 206 closed in last 90d; top contributor oliviertassinari at 22% of top-100 contributions; described as 'free forever'.

sources.title: shadcn-ui/ui — GitHub
sources.claim: shadcn/ui repo health as of 14 Jul 2026: 119,064 stars, MIT, 1,019 open issues, 150 opened / 53 closed in last 90d; user 'shadcn' accounts for 73% of top-100 contributions.

sources.title: mantinedev/mantine — GitHub
sources.claim: Mantine repo health as of 14 Jul 2026: 31,424 stars, MIT, only 12 open issues, 80 opened / 83 closed in last 90d; maintainer rtivital accounts for 94% of top-100 contributions (13,701 commits).

sources.title: mui/base-ui — GitHub
sources.claim: Base UI repo as of 14 Jul 2026: 10,335 stars, MIT, 311 open issues, 159 opened / 117 closed in last 90d; created Feb 2024; top human contributors atomiks (21%) and michaldudak (11%).

sources.title: radix-ui/primitives — GitHub
sources.claim: Radix Primitives (19,064 stars) is maintained by WorkOS following its acquisition of Modulz — relevant because shadcn/ui's former default primitive layer now sits under a different owner than Base UI.

sources.title: mui/mui-x — GitHub
sources.claim: MUI X repo as of 14 Jul 2026: 5,811 stars, no repo-level OSS license (dual-licensed packages), 1,552 open issues; latest @mui/x-data-grid is 9.9.0 (9 Jul 2026).

sources.title: npm — @mui/material
sources.claim: @mui/material latest is 9.2.0 (3 Jul 2026), MIT, with peer deps react ^17 || ^18 || ^19 and @emotion/react + @emotion/styled still required; v5/v6/v7 dist-tags remain published.

sources.title: npm — @base-ui/react
sources.claim: @base-ui/react latest is 1.6.0 (18 Jun 2026), MIT; 1.0.0 published 11 Dec 2025; peer deps react ^17 || ^18 || ^19; no CSS/styling dependency.

sources.title: npm — @mantine/core
sources.claim: @mantine/core latest is 9.4.1 (28 Jun 2026), MIT; peer dependency on react is a hard ^19.2.0 — no React 18 support path in Mantine 9.

sources.title: npm — shadcn (CLI)
sources.claim: The shadcn CLI's latest version is 4.13.0 (3 Jul 2026), MIT — it is a devDependency/codegen tool, not a runtime library.

sources.title: npm downloads API — @mui/material, Jun 2026
sources.claim: @mui/material had 38.66M npm downloads in June 2026, up from 27.49M in January 2026 — still the single largest React component library by download volume.

sources.title: npm downloads API — @mantine/core, Jun 2026
sources.claim: @mantine/core had 8.04M npm downloads in June 2026, up from 4.48M in January 2026 (1.8x) — growth below the ecosystem-wide baseline inflation.

sources.title: npm downloads API — @base-ui/react, Jun 2026
sources.claim: @base-ui/react had 24.90M npm downloads in June 2026, up from 1.75M in January 2026 — a 14x rise driven by shadcn/ui making Base UI its default primitive layer.

sources.title: npm downloads API — shadcn CLI, Jun 2026
sources.claim: The shadcn CLI had 22.11M npm downloads in June 2026, up from 3.35M in January 2026 (6.6x).

sources.title: MUI — Pricing
sources.claim: MUI X 2026 pricing: Community free (MIT), Pro $299/dev/yr, Premium $599/dev/yr, Enterprise $1,399/dev/yr with a 15-seat minimum. Licences are perpetual with 12 months of maintenance; renewals may rise up to 7% per year.

sources.title: MUI X — Licensing
sources.claim: MUI X feature gating: Pro adds multi-filtering, multi-sorting, column resizing and column pinning plus date-range pickers; Premium adds row grouping, aggregation and Excel export. Enforcement is runtime via LicenseInfo.setLicenseKey(); validation failure renders a watermark and logs a console warning in production, not just development. 30-day non-production trial.

sources.title: MUI blog — Introducing MUI v9
sources.claim: Material UI and MUI X v9 shipped together on 8 April 2026; Material UI went from v7 straight to v9 (no v8) to re-align its major version with MUI X. New in v9: NumberField, Menubar, CSS variables with color-mix(), Data Grid AI Assistant, candlestick charts, alpha Scheduler and Chat.

sources.title: MUI blog — 2026 and beyond
sources.claim: MUI's 2026 roadmap: Base UI is the major investment area; Pigment CSS is paused in alpha; Joy UI is on hold; Toolpad is not actively maintained; MUI Sync ceased in 2024. Emotion-independence and better Tailwind integration paths are stated as future work, not shipped.

sources.title: InfoQ — Base UI v1.0 ships 35 accessible components
sources.claim: Base UI v1.0 shipped with 35 accessible components, renamed its package from @base-ui-components/react to @base-ui/react, and is backed by MUI with dedicated engineers, designers and managers — explicitly positioned against post-acquisition uncertainty at Radix. Built by contributors from Radix, MUI and Floating UI.

sources.title: Base UI — Releases
sources.claim: Base UI release timeline: 1.0.0 stable on 11 Dec 2025, then 1.1.0 (Jan 2026), 1.2.0 (Feb, Drawer preview), 1.3.0 (Mar, Drawer stable), 1.4.0 (Apr, OTPField preview), 1.5.0 (May), 1.6.0 (Jun 2026, OTPField stable) — a steady monthly minor cadence with no breaking majors since 1.0.

sources.title: shadcn/ui changelog — Base UI is the default
sources.claim: As of July 2026, Base UI is the default primitive library in shadcn/ui: `shadcn init` selects Base UI, docs show Base UI first. Radix is not deprecated and remains available via `shadcn init -b radix`. Migration is offered as an AI-powered per-component skill rather than a codemod.

sources.title: shadcn/ui — Documentation
sources.claim: shadcn/ui explicitly rejects the component-library category and positions itself as a code distribution platform where the CLI copies source into your project.

sources.title: Mantine — 9.0.0 changelog
sources.claim: Mantine 9.0.0 released 31 March 2026; requires React 19.2+ for all @mantine/* packages; adds @mantine/schedule (calendar/scheduling), @mantine/mcp-server for AI agents, async form validation, and new components (FloatingWindow, OverflowList, Marquee, Scroller, BarsList).

sources.title: Mantine — official site
sources.claim: Mantine advertises 120+ components and 70 hooks, 500+ contributors, 30,000+ GitHub stars, 5M+ monthly downloads and 12,000+ Discord members; it is MIT and 'free forever for everyone' with no paid tier, and is built by Vitaly Rtishchev.

sources.title: Open Collective — mantinedev
sources.claim: Mantine's Open Collective shows an estimated annual budget of ~$18,540, $18,373 raised in total and 125 contributors, administered by Vitaly Rtishchev — i.e. the project has no commercial entity or salaried team behind it.

sources.title: MUI — About
sources.claim: MUI is a company founded in 2014 with a 100% remote team of 40+ people across 20+ countries.

sources.title: Crunchbase — MUI
sources.claim: MUI (the Paris-based company behind Material UI) has raised no venture funding — it is bootstrapped, financed by MUI X Pro/Premium licence revenue.

sources.title: shadcn on X — joining Vercel as a design engineer
sources.claim: shadcn (Shadab Ahmed) joined Vercel as a design engineer in August 2023 to continue building open-source UI components — shadcn/ui is therefore Vercel-adjacent, funded by a salary rather than by the project itself.

sources.title: State of React 2025 — component libraries
sources.claim: State of React 2025 (~2,600 respondents): MUI is still #1 in usage among component libraries while shadcn/ui grows fast and is close to overtaking it; a large share of respondents use no component library at all, indicating the space is not settled.

sources.title: npm downloads API — @radix-ui/react-dialog, Jun 2026
sources.claim: @radix-ui/react-dialog grew from 65.8M (Jan 2026) to 247.4M (Jun 2026) monthly downloads — a 3.8x rise despite Radix being displaced as shadcn/ui's default, showing that 2026 npm download growth is heavily inflated and must be read as a relative baseline, not as adoption.

sources.title: npm — @base-ui-components/react (frozen scope)
sources.claim: The pre-1.0 Base UI package scope @base-ui-components/react is frozen at 1.0.0-rc.0 (4 Dec 2025) yet still pulls ~400k downloads/week — pre-2026 tutorials and snippets point at the dead scope.
